newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mixed, August up on export talk.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mixed, August up on export talk.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed mixed on Thursday, with August up sharply amid talk of increased demand for old-crop supplies, pit sources said.
"They're talking about shifting beans from Brazil to U.S. origin," said Vic Lespinasse, a trader with Dean Witter. "But the six- to 10-day (forecast) was bearish for new crop."

Indications are that a cargo of soybeans sold by Brazil for August shipment was switched to U.S. origin, trade and U.S. export sources said. There was talk the soybeans were sent to Europe out of the Great Lakes.
USDA export data also boosted old-crop months.

USDA put weekly export sales at 158,300 tonnes, above expectations. Some trade sources noted soybean sales have exceeded USDA's projection for 890 million bushels for the current crop year, but analysts said buyers would likely cancel some purchases or switch to new crop, keeping exports within USDA's projections.

"As long as the crop maintains itself in the fields, the odds of cancellations and rollovers increase," said John Kleist, analyst with Sagamore Partners. "Why pay the premium for old crop if you're going to have a record new crop?"
Soybeans ended 13 cents per bushel higher to 1-3/4 cents lower with August up 13 at $7.52.

New crop months closed lower amid bearishly construed weather forecasts. The National Weather Service six- to 10-day weather outlook called for normal to below normal temperatures and normal to above normal rainfall. That scenario allayed fears that persistent hot, dry weather would damage crops.

On the day, commercials were noted buyers of the August which supported talk of export business. ADM bought one million bushels August, Cargill Inc bough 1.5 million August and Continental Grain bought one million August, pit sources said. Commercials were also key stoppers of deliveries.

In spread action, Continental bull spread 1.6 million August/November at $1.47 to $1.45, premium August. Lind-Waldock, LFG, Term Commodities and Cargill were also noted August/November bull spreaders.

In options, Goldenberg-Hehmeyer bought 700 November $6.00 puts and sold 1,400 November $5.75 puts at one to 1-1/2 cents, Smith Barney bought 500 September $5.75 puts at 3/4 cent and ADM sold 100 November $6.00 calls at 25 cents.
Volatility in the November slipped to 22 percent, from 23-1/2 percent on Wednesday.

Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 35,000 contracts, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 43,143 contracts. Options volume was pegged at 12,000 contracts, against Wednesday's 11,777.
